subject: music
topicDisplay: Component 1 Listening Western And World Music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a pop song, the section that repeats with the same words and main 'hook' is the:
questions.explain: The chorus repeats with the same lyrics and usually contains the song's main hook.

questions.q: In a DAW, 'automation' is most commonly used to:
options: Make settings like volume or panning change automatically over time
questions.explain: Automation lets parameters such as volume or panning change automatically across a track over time.

questions.q: A plagal cadence (often called the 'Amen' cadence) is:
questions.explain: A plagal cadence moves from chord IV to chord I.

questions.q: On a string instrument, the technique 'pizzicato' means to:
options: Pluck the strings with the finger
questions.explain: Pizzicato instructs the player to pluck the strings rather than bow them.

questions.q: Rock and pop since the 1960s is most associated with which line-up?
questions.explain: Modern rock and pop is typically built around guitars, bass, drums and vocals.

questions.q: How many beats does a dotted minim last in 4/4 time?
questions.explain: A dot adds half the note's value, so a minim (2 beats) plus its dot (1 beat) lasts three beats.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the term 'raga' refers to:
options: A set of notes (melodic framework) used to create a melody
questions.explain: A raga is the melodic framework, a chosen set of notes, on which a performer improvises.

questions.q: A minim is worth how many crotchet beats?
questions.explain: A minim is worth two crotchet beats.

questions.q: The steel pan (steel drum) is a tuned percussion instrument from:
questions.explain: The steel pan originated in Trinidad and is central to Caribbean music.

questions.q: Which structure follows the pattern ABA?
questions.explain: Ternary form has three sections in an ABA pattern, where the A material returns.

questions.q: A chromatic scale moves entirely in:
questions.explain: A chromatic scale ascends or descends entirely in semitones, using all twelve pitches.

questions.q: Reverb, delay and distortion are examples of audio:
questions.explain: Reverb, delay and distortion are audio effects used to alter a sound.

questions.q: In the mnemonic 'MAD T-SHIRT' for the elements of music, what does the 'I' stand for?
questions.explain: In 'MAD T-SHIRT' the I stands for instrumentation, meaning the choice of instruments and voices used.

questions.q: A triad in 'first inversion' has which note in the bass?
questions.explain: In first inversion the third of the chord is the lowest sounding note.

questions.q: What does the time signature 3/4 tell you?
options: Three beats in a bar, each a quaver
Three beats in a bar, each a crotchet
Four beats in a bar, each a crotchet
questions.explain: In 3/4 there are three crotchet beats per bar, giving a waltz feel.

questions.q: A sharp sign in front of a note does what?
options: Raises the pitch by a semitone
Lowers the pitch by a semitone
questions.explain: A sharp raises a note's pitch by one semitone.

questions.q: A 'power chord' on an electric guitar typically consists of:
options: The root and its fifth (and octave)
A full major triad with seventh
All seven notes of a scale
questions.explain: A power chord uses the root and the fifth (often plus the octave), common in rock.

questions.q: When performing in an ensemble, watching a conductor or leader mainly helps players to:
options: Stay together in time and respond to changes
questions.explain: Following a conductor or leader keeps the ensemble together in time and unified in expression.

questions.q: Which group of instruments typically forms the 'rhythm section' of a band?
questions.explain: The rhythm section usually consists of drums, bass and a chordal instrument like guitar or keyboard.

questions.q: Which time signature is an example of compound time?
questions.explain: 6/8 is compound time because each beat divides into three quavers (two dotted-crotchet beats).

questions.q: A recurring musical theme linked to a character, place or idea in film or opera is a:
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a recurring theme associated with a character, place or idea.

questions.q: Which musical period came first?
questions.explain: The Baroque period (c1600-1750) came before the Classical period.
